## Motivation

- Generate block-level kv_indices directly in create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton
  by passing PAGED_SIZE=page_size, eliminating the per-step
  _transform_table_1_to_real overhead (tensor alloc + gather + div + copy)
- Use launch_reshape_and_cache_flash for non-SWA models to fuse K/V cache
  writes into a single Triton kernel instead of two separate scatter ops

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Benchmarking and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

This pull request introduces significant optimizations for non-Sliding Window Attention (SWA) models within the unified attention mechanism. The primary goal is to enhance performance by streamlining the generation of KV cache indices and broadening the application of an optimized KV cache write function. These changes ensure that non-SWA models can leverage more efficient block-level indexing directly, leading to improved overall efficiency in attention computations and KV cache management. ### Highlights * **Optimized KV Index Generation for Non-SWA Models**: The logic for generating KV cache indices has been refined for models not using Sliding Window Attention (non-SWA). Instead of generating token-level indices and then transforming them, these models now directly generate block-level indices, leading to more efficient memory access and processing. * **Expanded `reshape_and_cache_flash` Usage**: The `reshape_and_cache_flash` function, responsible for writing KV cache, is now utilized for all unified attention models, not just those employing Sliding Window Attention. `bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces optimizations for unified attention on AMD GPUs, specifically for non-SWA (Sliding Window Attention) models. The changes are well-implemented and focus on two main areas:

1.  **Optimized index generation**: For non-SWA models, the code now directly generates block-level `kv_indices` instead of creating token-level indices and then transforming them. This is achieved by modifying the call to the `create_flashmla_kv_indices_triton` kernel. This optimization is consistently applied across `init_forward_metadata`, `init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph`, and `init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph` functions.
2.  **Optimized KV cache write**: The `launch_reshape_and_cache_flash` function is now utilized for non-SWA models, extending its use beyond just SWA models. The SWA-specific logic is correctly guarded, ensuring that non-SWA paths do not execute SWA-related code. This change is applied in both `forward_extend` and `forward_decode` methods.

Additionally, the pull request includes a minor but effective optimization by moving the creation of `page_indices` into the conditional block where it is used, avoiding unnecessary computation.

The changes are clear, consistent, and appear to correctly implement the intended optimizations. I have not found any issues or bugs in the implementation.
